newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS Swiss restructuring seen as moderate.
newsitem.headline: UBS Swiss restructuring seen as moderate.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland, the country's biggest bank, is expected to unveil plans next Tuesday for cutting costs by streamlining domestic operations but without dramatic job cuts.

Analysts said the UBS autumn news conference on November 26 was expected to detail plans promised in July for merging some administration and production centres and trimming bank branches and services.
The reorganisation would be more moderate than steps by UBS's Swiss rivals this year that involved thousands of job cuts on the domestic side, analysts added.
"I do not think it will be any reason to lower my cost estimates for UBS," said Madeleine Hofmann at CS Research.
"The cost estimates are already fairly low because I have already taken into account what they could be expected to do on the Swiss domestic side," she told Reuters.

Hofmann said she expected UBS to reduce the number of administrative areas in its Swiss network, consolidate domestic production centres from eight to as few as three, close some smaller branches and reduce services at others.
Claudia von Tuerk at Geneva-based Pictet & Cie said UBS did not need to make huge cuts like the other two banks, CS Holding and Swiss Bank Corp, because it had been gradually trimming all along.
The banks are retrenching following a downturn in the Swiss economy which has led to a sharp rise in defaults.
"They may be streamlining in Switzerland, but I don't think it will be a major announcement. UBS has been doing its homework," she said.
UBS chief executive Mathias Cabiallavetta noted recently that the banking group had cut its Swiss workforce by 1,700 since 1992 and closed about 80 branches in the past five years.

Von Tuerk said the Swiss stock market may have overlooked some of these steps by UBS to cut its cost base because the moves were quieter than its rival's dramatic announcements of branch closings and job cuts.
"The news conference could give UBS a chance to present what it has done so far to streamline Swiss operations and announce a few more measures as a way of drawing the market's attention," she said.
UBS itself declines to go farther than describing the news conference in general terms.
"We will talk about restructuring in the Swiss region," UBS spokeswoman Gertrud Erismann said and would not elaborate.
But analysts noted that UBS last July confirmed it was drawing up plans to reduce costs in domestic operations in a fashion similar to the way it has altered the bank's structure at the group level.

The bank said at the time it was studying how to reduce the 31 so-called "economic areas" that make up its domestic network. The economic areas correspond to Switzerland's cantons, with a few exceptions.
The domestic business would also be restructured into three divisions -- retail, corporate and private banking -- UBS said in July.
But UBS said then that newspaper reports were "exaggerated" in saying the plans would result in the closure of a large number of branches and in massive job cuts.

SBC in September announced a sweeping restructuring of its domestic operations including shedding some 1,700 jobs, or 10 percent of its Swiss workforce, while CS Holding said in July it would slash 3,500 Swiss jobs plus 1,500 worldwide.
